text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like BABA on 2026-09-18, the median 5-session forward return was 0.05%, with outcomes split exactly evenly between gains and losses. The single number to anchor on is that median: this state has historically produced no directional edge over a one-week horizon, and the engine's own validation confirms it does not beat a naive benchmark.

[state]
The retrieval pulled these 50 analogs because BABA is sitting in a deep short-term hole while the broader market is flat. The most distinctive features are distance from 52-week high at -41.23% (z-score -1.798), 20-session return vs benchmark at -13.37% (z-score -1.459), and raw 20-session return at -13.25% (z-score -1.442). Volatility is elevated at 42.99% annualised (z-score 0.685), and WTI crude surged 19.24% over 20 days (z-score 1.124). The event feature shows calendar days to next earnings release capped at 45 days (z-score 0.663), meaning the engine found states matching this technical setup rather than isolating immediate pre-earnings sessions. These features, weighted 30% to name-level price action and 20% each to macro and event context, pulled 30 distinct symbols across 37 distinct sessions into the neighborhood.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of 0.96% and a median of 0.05%, with a standard deviation of 6.64%. Exactly 50% of the episodes finished above zero and 50% below. The distribution is slightly right-skewed (0.321) but fat-tailed on both sides, ranging from -20.44% to 21.43%. The 10th percentile was -4.76% and the 90th percentile was 7.87%. The bad tail is dominated by recent technology and China ADR names: AVGO on 2026-09-08 returned -7.95%, META on 2026-08-13 returned -8.26%, NKE on 2026-09-03 returned -5.08%, and BABA itself on 2026-09-08 returned -2.95%. The good tail is driven by outliers like NIO on 2025-07-08 (+21.43%) and INTC on 2025-08-11 (+14.58%). Note that only 2 of the 50 analogs were BABA itself; the rest are cross-sectional matches.

[tails]
A position can end near the median and still be un-holdable through the week. Across the 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -2.11%, and the 10th percentile of max adverse excursion reached -5.89%. In 24% of the episodes, the path breached a 5% drawdown intra-horizon. A 10% drawdown was breached in 2% of cases, a 15% drawdown in 2%, and a 20% drawdown in 2%. The median max favourable excursion was 2.87%, yielding a reward-risk ratio of 1.36. The 90% value-at-risk on the endpoint was 4.76%, and the conditional VaR was 9.52%.

[stress]
The baseline median across all 50 analogs is 0.05%. Several stress scenarios materially worsen that picture. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario (48 analogs) produced a median of -4.32%, a delta of -4.37% versus baseline, and a 52.1% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, and it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast. The 2025-04 tariff shock scenario (26 analogs) yielded a median of -3.8%, a delta of -3.85%, and a 42.3% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare (50 analogs) gave a median of -3.26% (delta -3.31%), with an 88% probability of holding within a 10% drawdown; caveat: ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters late-window analogs. The 2022 inflation/rate bear (50 analogs) showed a median of -3.32% (delta -3.37%); caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly. The earnings release day shock (50 analogs) produced a median of -0.95% (delta -1.0%); caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The weekend hold on the 7x24 venue (50 analogs) gave a median of -0.2% (delta -0.25%); caveat: blocks are paired to analogs by index modulo the block count, a deterministic convention, not a joint distribution, and a perpetual carries funding and basis a spot token does not. No scenarios were skipped.

[reasoning]
The three scenarios most relevant to buying BABA into earnings are: first, the earnings release day shock, because it directly conditions on the catalyst you asked about, showing a median of -0.95% (delta -1.0%) across 50 analogs with a 12% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Second, the 2025-04 tariff shock, because BABA is a China ADR and this scenario isolates trade-exposed policy risk, producing a median of -3.8% (delta -3.85%) across 26 analogs with a 30.8% probability of falling more than 10%. Third, the 2020-02/03 liquidity crash, because it represents the worst-case cross-asset deleveraging for a volatile name, yielding a median of -4.32% (delta -4.37%) across 48 analogs with a 52.1% breach probability. A concentration to distrust is the heavy weighting of 2025 (23 analogs) and 2026 (16 analogs) in the retrieval set, meaning the distribution is overwhelmingly driven by very recent market regimes rather than long-term history. No scenario contradicts the direction of a long idea outright, as every stress median is negative or near zero, but none supports a reliable positive expectation either.

[limits]
This analysis describes a historical conditional distribution, not a forecast. The honest verdict from the engine's validation is explicit: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The directional hit rate is 50.1%. For path risk, the engine targets a 10% drawdown level. Out of sample, the realised breach rate was 2%, while the mean predicted rate from the analog excursion share was 3.4%, producing a calibration gap of 1.4 percentage points (clustered standard error 0.48 pp). The analog Brier score for path risk was 0.0196. Paired differences against the volatility reflection benchmark (0.0241), same-name calibration (0.024), and pooled calibration (0.021) all have 95% confidence intervals that exclude zero, meaning the analog breach probabilities are statistically better calibrated than those alternatives on this build. Regarding the wrapper: if you trade this outside cash hours, you are trading a tokenised instrument. Status is measured. On the primary Bitget RWA perpetual (BABA/USDT), the reference market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 67.32% of the wrapper's own hourly movement landed in those closed hours. It is a tight tracker with a return correlation of 0.9781 and tracking error of 60 bp/day. The basis band is -0.19% to 0.67%, and the spread is 5.34 bps. Caveat: a tight perpetual is not the underlying and not a redeemable spot token; it carries idiosyncratic risk, funding applies, and the basis means your exit price differs from the reference close the analog distribution uses. The closed-session return layer, measured over 6 weekend blocks, shows a median weekend return of -1.185%, a 10th percentile of -1.7235%, a standard deviation of 1.647%, and a median intra-weekend adverse excursion of -1.551%. In 16.7% of those 6 weekends, the wrapper breached a 5% drawdown while the US cash market was shut. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was closed, and they are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
